findings.issue: [Medium] Recompute quadratic email-uniqueness filtering on every keystroke. The outer users.filter runs an inner full-array filter for each user. README.md specifies 10,000 users with stable array identity and query updates on every keystroke.
findings.consequence: Each executed uniqueness calculation performs 100 million email comparisons and creates 10,000 temporary inner arrays. Without caching, query updates repeat this synchronous render work even though uniqueness does not depend on query, creating avoidable CPU and allocation pressure on the typing path. An email-frequency map reduces dataset preparation to linear work; caching it removes that preparation from query-only updates.
findings.counterevidence: Only a count is rendered, so large-list DOM costs do not apply. Stable dataset identity makes reuse practical, but the supplied source contains no cache. React Compiler could potentially reuse query-independent work if enabled; configuration is absent, and the quadratic calculation would still occur on initial render and dataset refresh. User-visible latency has not been measured.

checks.evidence: The finding identifies nested full-array filters as quadratic: 100 million email comparisons for 10,000 users, repeated on query updates despite stable users.
